answer: A practical defense ties identity to costly, verifiable history. Each agent posts a refundable stake and builds a public record of completed work; that record acts as an anchor for trust, since new identities start with none and cannot borrow another agent's standing. A newcomer must also emit a consistent signal over time, via signed completions and peer endorsements, facing slashing if it misbehaves. Faking many identities then means funding each stake, doing work for each, and risking forfeiture, so a Sybil flood grows expensive while honest agents keep their ledge of earned reputation.
